description: We are IoT Avengers, a NASA Space Apps Global Nominee team passionate about AI, space technology, and Earth observation. We enjoy building innovative solutions and learning together. We're looking for passionate teammates skilled in coding, AI/ML, data science, UI/UX, and creative problem-solving to collaborate, innovate, and make an impact.
summary:
SARC is a satellite-based geospatial research platform developed during the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026. It studies environmental changes around the Teesta River Basin in Sikkim, focusing on the downstream region of Singtam–Majitar–Rangpo, following the 4 October 2023 South Lhonak Lake disaster.

The project uses Sentinel-1 and NISAR satellite data through two separate analysis workflows to examine changes in radar observations over selected areas. It also includes a Flutter-based mobile application as a user-facing component.

SARC aims to make satellite-based environmental analysis more accessible and support the study of areas that may be exposed to flood-related impacts. The current version is a research prototype, not an operational flood forecasting or early-warning system. It demonstrates how satellite observations and geospatial analysis can contribute to better understanding of vulnerable river regions.
details:
SARC is a geospatial research platform designed to study environmental changes in flood-prone Himalayan River regions using satellite observations.

The project focuses on the Teesta River Basin in Sikkim, particularly the Singtam–Majitar–Rangpo region, following the South Lhonak Lake disaster of 4 October 2023.

SARC uses two separate satellite analysis workflows. The Sentinel-1A workflow compares radar observations from 2 October and 14 October 2023 to identify candidate areas of surface change. The NISAR S-band workflow analyses three 2026 acquisitions using HH/HV polarimetric data, statistical features, clustering and anomaly analysis. These workflows are independently processed, and their outputs are not presented as a validated combined flood map.

The project also includes a Flutter-based mobile application to provide a user-facing interface. The team used Python, Google Colab, ESA SNAP, geospatial processing libraries and Flutter during development.

SARC is creative in bringing multiple radar observation approaches into one research platform while keeping their analyses distinct. It demonstrates how satellite data can help researchers study environmental changes in difficult-to-access regions. The current version is a research prototype; operational forecasting would require regular data updates, further integration and ground-based validation.
